benchmarks.note: Land benchmarks: residential ¥/tsubo by station, MLIT transaction data via Utinokati (2023–2025) cross-checked against 2026 official residential land-price points: Kashiwanoha-Campus ~68 (the raw ~75 station figure carries a station-front lift), Kashiwa ~65 (the all-use total of ~108 mixes station-front commercial plots and is not used), Minami-Kashiwa ~56, Shin-Kashiwa ~54, Kashiwa-Tanaka ~54 (a ~97 station-front point is commercial), Toyoshiki ~50, Kita-Kashiwa ~45 (the raw ~34 is dragged down by fringe and very large lots), Masuo ~42, Edogawadai ~35 (scored on the Kashiwa side of the station; the ~47 all-use total is Nagareyama-side), Takayanagi ~34 (a '2026' district print of 2.9 rests on exactly one deal and is ignored), Sakasai ~30 (raw ~25, fringe drag). Urbanisation-control transactions (~¥7万/tsubo) are never blended into any figure — the east of the city is a different legal market where building is in principle prohibited. Walk bands use the city's own transaction walk-band averages; genuine residential lots ease roughly 10–15% by an 11–15-minute walk. Used houses transacted at about ¥100万/tsubo city-wide (floor-area basis), with age the dominant adjustment: stock under 10 years old ~129, 30+-year stock ~59. Official residential land prices rose +5.18% in the 2026 公示地価 survey (+4.70% in 基準地価) — a fifth consecutive rise, fastest at Kashiwanoha-Campus (+7.85%).
